# Use Case: View Veterinarians

## Overview

**Use Case ID:** UC-002   
**Use Case Name:** View Veterinarians   
**Primary Actor:** Visitor   
**Goal:** Browse the list of veterinarians employed at the clinic along with their specialties.   
**Status:** Approved   
**Requirements:** [FR-003, NFR-001, NFR-002, NFR-003, C-010, C-011](../requirements.md)

## Preconditions

- At least one veterinarian is recorded in the system (see A1 otherwise).

## Main Success Scenario

1. Visitor clicks the "Veterinarians" link in the navigation bar.
2. System retrieves the first set of veterinarians.
3. System renders the veterinarians grid showing, for each vet, the first name, last name, and a comma-separated list of
   specialties (or "none" if no specialties are held).
4. As the Visitor scrolls toward the end of the grid, the system fetches and appends the next chunk of veterinarians
   until all entries have been loaded.

## Alternative Flows

### A1: No Veterinarians Registered

**Trigger:** The clinic has no veterinarians recorded (step 2).
**Flow:**

1. System renders the veterinarians grid with no rows.
2. Use case ends.

### Success Postconditions

- The veterinarians grid is rendered with all loaded entries.
- No data is modified.

### Failure Postconditions

- On data-access errors, the application error view is shown and no vet list is displayed.

2	
3	Read this **before writing or modifying any test** under `src/test/java/`.

5	## Two test layers — the class suffix picks the Maven phase
6	
7	| Layer                 | Suffix  | Runs in         | Framework                                              | Skill                               |
8	|-----------------------|---------|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------|
9	| Server-side view test | `*Test` | `./mvnw test`   | Vaadin Browserless (`SpringBrowserlessTest`)           | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` |
10	| Browser test          | `*IT`   | `./mvnw verify` | Playwright + Drama Finder (`AbstractBasePlaywrightIT`) | `aiup-vaadin-jooq:playwright-test`  |
11	
12	Surefire picks up `*Test`, Failsafe picks up `*IT` (both configured via `spring-boot-starter-parent`; the failsafe
13	plugin is declared in `pom.xml`). A browserless test named `*IT` or a Playwright test named `*Test` runs in the wrong
14	phase, and `TestLayerConventionsTest` fails the build when one does. The rule is worth enforcing because the
15	failure is otherwise silent: nothing errors, the wrong Maven plugin simply never picks the class up, and a test
16	that never runs reports as passing. Browserless is the default for use cases; Playwright is for test cases (`TC-*`) and
17	anything that genuinely needs a browser (client-side rendering, keyboard focus, scrolling).
18	
19	## Framework
20	
21	- **Vaadin Browserless Testing** (`browserless-test-junit6` + `browserless-test-spring`) is the default for Vaadin view
22	  tests — server-side, no
23	  browser, no servlet container.
24	  Reference: https://vaadin.com/docs/latest/flow/testing/browserless/getting-started
25	- View tests extend `PetClinicTestBase` (or `SpringBrowserlessTest` directly for tests that don't touch the DB, in
26	  which case add `@SpringBootTest` and `@Import(TestcontainersConfiguration.class)` yourself).
27	  They run inside a Spring context and use the same Testcontainers Postgres as the rest of the tests.
28	- **Use the `aiup-vaadin-jooq:browserless-test` skill** to scaffold a browserless test for a use case. Prefer it over
29	  hand-rolling — it knows the conventions in this file (locators, `@UseCase`, naming, etc.).
30	- **Karibu is gone.** Any `com.github.mvysny.kaributesting.*` import is a mistake — the project is all
31	  `SpringBrowserlessTest` / `ComponentQuery` now. The `karibu-test` skill is obsolete.
32	
33	## Test class naming — `UC<NNN><UseCaseName>Test`
34	
35	Tests that verify a use case are named after the use case, **not** the view. Format:
36	`UC<NNN><UseCaseNameInPascalCase>Test`, e.g `UC001ViewWelcomePageTest`, `UC004FindOwnersByLastNameTest`,
37	`UC007AddPetToOwnerTest`. The `NNN` matches the `UC-NNN-*.md` file in `docs/use_cases/`.

43	[`development.md`](development.md)) and `PetclinicApplicationTests` verify no single use case, so they sit in the

- **Updates are last-write-wins.** No version column, no optimistic locking. Two
  clerks editing one record: the later save silently wins. No use case asks for
  more, and adding it would change the use cases that update — so it is a
  specification change first and a code change second.

- **No pessimistic locks, no `SELECT … FOR UPDATE`.**

## Synchronous and asynchronous processing

Everything is synchronous, inside the user's request:

| Mechanism                      | Used? |
|--------------------------------|-------|
| Batch jobs / schedulers        | no    |
| Message queues / domain events | no    |
| `@Async`, background threads   | no    |
| Vaadin `@Push` / server push   | no    |
| Caching layer                  | no    |

An agent must not introduce any of them to solve a problem the specification
does not pose. If a use case ever needs one, it changes this table and gets an
ADR.

## Query cost

- **Unbounded lists load lazily** ([GR-002](../business_rules.md#gr-002-lazy-loading-of-lists),
  NFR-001/002): `findPage(offset, limit)` plus
  a paired `count()`, wired as a Vaadin callback data provider. Rows fetched per
  scroll step do not grow with the table size.
- **To-many data in a lazy grid is pre-joined with `multiset(...)`** so a grid
  never issues a query per row — the owner search results with their pet names
  (UC-004) and the vet directory with its specialties (UC-002).
- **Indexes carrying this:** `owners_last_name_idx` (prefix search),
  `pets_owner_name_unique` (leads with `owner_id`, so it serves the lookups by
  owner as well as the uniqueness check), `visits_pet_id_idx`.

## Failure paths

| At runtime                                  | Result                                                  |
|---------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|
----
| Ordering of a list                    | an `ORDER BY` in the query that feeds it — never a sort in the view |
| Reachability of a route               | the view's `beforeEnter`, which throws `NotFoundException` when the entity does not fit the route |

**Validation is not in the domain records.** Domain types are plain records with
no annotations and no constructor checks — the form is the validation boundary.

## Reference data

`VET`, `SPECIALTY`, `VET_SPECIALTY` and `PET_TYPE` are reference data: the
practice maintains them directly in the database and the application only reads
them (C-011). That is a modelling fact with a structural consequence — those
modules need read queries and no write path. An agent asked for a "manage
specialties" screen is being asked for something outside the current scope.

trajectory.message:
UC-002 (View Veterinarians) is implemented at `/vets`, and the full `./mvnw test` run passes: 65 tests, including the ArchUnit rules and the four traceability sensors.

I read the spec and the architecture docs first and followed them. Docker isn't running here, but the repo's local-Postgres path (`vb-postgres`) worked, so the jOOQ codegen and the DB-backed tests ran for real.

**What was added**
- `vet/domain/Vet.java`: a `Serializable` record with id, names, and the specialty list.
- `vet/domain/VetRepository.java`: `@Repository` with class-level `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`. `findPage(offset, limit)` fetches the vets and their specialties in one query via `multiset`, and `count()` backs the grid's size.
- `vet/ui/VetsView.java`: `@Route("vets")` inside `MainLayout`. It's a grid with First Name, Last Name and Specialties columns, fed by a callback data provider, so rows load as the user scrolls. A vet with no specialties shows "none".
- `src/test/.../vet/ui/UC002ViewVeterinariansTest.java`: five browserless tests, each tagged `@UseCase`. They cover the main scenario, A1 (no vets), BR-001 (lazy loading, with 30 extra vets so the last row is fetched on demand), BR-002 (alphabetical specialties), and BR-003 (anonymous access).

**Choices I made where the spec was silent**
- **Vet order:** the spec only orders specialties. GR-003 requires every list to have a defined order, so vets sort by last name, first name, then id. The id tiebreak keeps paging stable.
- **Specialty formatting:** a comma-separated list, as TC-006 expects ("dentistry, surgery").

**Not done**
- **Status line:** I left UC-002 at `Approved`. Setting `Done` switches on the coverage sensor, and the spec says to run `aiup-vaadin-jooq:coverage-check` before changing it. That skill isn't in my available skill list, so I couldn't run the audit. The tests above already cover the main scenario, A1, and all three business rules, so the audit should be a formality.
- **TC-006:** it stays `Approved`. Its Playwright `TC006…IT` class would be a separate piece of work.
